description: You are an archaeoastronomer studying the astronomical alignments of Stonehenge. Your research requires simulating the summer solstice sunrise as it would have appeared from Stonehenge around 2500 BCE, when the main sarsen circle was erected. Configure Stellarium for Stonehenge (latitude 51.1789°N, longitude 1.8262°W, altitude 102m). Navigate to June 21, 2500 BCE and set the time to approximately 04:45 UTC (local pre-sunrise time in midsummer England). Configure the display for this research scenario: enable the atmosphere (for authentic dawn sky colors and horizon refraction), disable the landscape ground (for unobstructed horizon view), enable the azimuthal coordinate grid (for precise sunrise azimuth measurements), and enable the equatorial coordinate grid (to record the Sun's celestial coordinates for your paper). Find the Sun using the search function, center on it, and take a screenshot documenting the pre-dawn sky. Write your research findings to /home/ga/Desktop/stonehenge_alignment.txt, including the observation location (Stonehenge), the date (June 21, 2500 BCE), and your observations about the solstice sunrise alignment.

metadata.data_source: Ordnance Survey / English Heritage; Darvill et al. (2012) Antiquity 86:1021-1040
